<h2>BIM Modeling &amp; Coordination</h2>

<p>
I build coordinated Revit models and take them through a full
<strong>architectural → structural → MEP → Navisworks</strong> workflow:
model every discipline, federate them, find the clashes, fix them in Revit,
and re-run until the model is clear. Then produce the drawings and schedules
straight from that model.
</p>

<p>
The five projects below are self-directed practice projects. Each is a
realistic building scope, small enough to take from levels and grids to a
final coordinated model, and chosen to exercise a different part of the
workflow.
</p>

## Workflow

Every project follows the same coordination loop. Clashes are resolved in the
authoring model, not in Navisworks, and the test is re-run until it comes back clear.

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/svg/bim-workflow.svg" width="100%" alt="BIM coordination workflow from levels and grids to documentation" />
</p>

1. **Set up:** levels, grids, views and project template
2. **Architectural:** walls, floors, roof, doors, windows, rooms
3. **Structural:** columns, beams, slabs, foundations
4. **MEP:** HVAC, plumbing, electrical and lighting
5. **Federate:** link the architectural, structural and MEP models, then open them together in Navisworks
6. **Clash detection:** run Clash Detective (e.g. pipe vs. beam, duct vs. slab), then review and group the results
7. **Resolve:** fix each clash in Revit, then re-run the test until it is clear
8. **Deliver:** sheets, sections, elevations, schedules and the final coordinated model

## Projects

### 01 · 2-Story Residential House

<p align="center"><img src="assets/svg/project-01-residential.svg" width="100%" alt="Project 01 — 2-story residential house" /></p>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Size** | ~200–250 m², 2 levels |
| **Software** | Autodesk Revit, Navisworks |
| **Program** | Living room, kitchen, 3 bedrooms, 2–3 bathrooms, staircase, small balcony, simple roof |

The full professional workflow on a compact building. I set up levels and grids,
modeled the architecture and basic structure, and added simple plumbing and HVAC.
Then I linked the three discipline models into Navisworks. There I planted and found
test clashes (pipe vs. beam), fixed them in Revit, re-ran the test, and issued the
final coordinated model with sheets, sections, elevations and schedules.

### 02 · 3-Story Office Building

<p align="center"><img src="assets/svg/project-02-office.svg" width="100%" alt="Project 02 — 3-story office building" /></p>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Size** | ~1,000–1,500 m², 3 levels |
| **Software** | Autodesk Revit, Navisworks |
| **Program** | Reception/lobby, open offices, meeting and conference rooms, toilets, stair, elevator, mechanical/electrical rooms, flat roof |

A step up from the house: more room types, families and schedules, plus a vertical
core that MEP services have to route around. Workflow: architectural → structural →
MEP → Navisworks coordination → clash detection → clash resolution → drawings and
schedules → final coordinated model.

### 03 · Single-Story Retail Store

<p align="center"><img src="assets/svg/project-03-retail.svg" width="100%" alt="Project 03 — single-story retail store" /></p>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Size** | ~300–500 m², 1 level |
| **Software** | Autodesk Revit, Navisworks |
| **Program** | Entrance and storefront, sales area, storage, office, staff room, toilets, mechanical/electrical room |

Focused on commercial detailing: storefront, ceilings, lighting, HVAC and plumbing.
The ceiling zone is where most of the coordination happens. Custom Revit families
were built for the fit-out before the model went through Navisworks clash detection
and resolution.

### 04 · 4-Story Apartment Building

<p align="center"><img src="assets/svg/project-04-apartment.svg" width="100%" alt="Project 04 — 4-story apartment building" /></p>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Size** | ~1,500–2,500 m², 4 levels, 12–20 apartments |
| **Software** | Autodesk Revit, Navisworks |
| **Program** | Residential floors, corridors and lobby, stair and elevator, parking, electrical and mechanical rooms, roof |

Repeating units and stacked services. The architectural model was coordinated with
structure, then plumbing, HVAC and electrical were added. Unit and room schedules
come straight from the model. Navisworks clash detection and resolution then led to
a construction documentation set.

### 05 · 2-Story Medical Clinic

<p align="center"><img src="assets/svg/project-05-clinic.svg" width="100%" alt="Project 05 — 2-story medical clinic" /></p>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Size** | ~1,000–1,500 m², 2 levels |
| **Software** | Autodesk Revit, Navisworks |
| **Program** | Reception, waiting areas, examination and treatment rooms, offices, toilets, storage, mechanical/electrical rooms |

The most demanding coordination of the set. Healthcare buildings pack far more MEP
into the same ceiling space, so this is where the clash-and-resolve loop gets the
heaviest use. I modeled the architecture and structure, developed the MEP systems,
coordinated all disciplines in Navisworks, resolved clashes, and produced schedules,
construction drawings and the final coordinated model.

## Portfolio website (MERN)

The same content is also a full-stack site: React (Vite) front end, Express API,
MongoDB for project content and contact-form messages.

```bash
npm install
npm run build     # build the React client
npm start         # http://localhost:5000
npm run dev       # live-reload development: http://localhost:5173
```

Configure the server in `server/.env` (see `server/.env.example`):

- `MONGODB_URI`: local MongoDB or Atlas. The projects are seeded automatically into an empty database.
- `MEMORY_DB=0`: run without a database. Content comes from the seed data and the contact form is disabled.
- `ADMIN_TOKEN`: read contact messages with `GET /api/messages` and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Reference photos on the site are openly licensed (CC0) and credited in
[assets/images/stock/CREDITS.md](assets/images/stock/CREDITS.md). They show real buildings and
construction work for context, and are not images of the portfolio projects themselves.
